top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a distinct, verified achievement: the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, in which the trap shift cancels between the two clock states so many neutral atoms are interrogated at once. It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and independent laboratories (RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) agree at the 10^-18 level, so the maturity is established. Katori and Ye is a compact allocation, and the citation should stay on the lattice and magic-wavelength idea, not on accuracy records or the redefinition of the second. P002 follows because it contains the same clock part but adds a single-name IceCube credit for a large collaboration, which I cannot judge well and find unsettled. P003 is a sound AMO prize, but it omits Dalibard and Cirac and I rank it below the clock; any award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Long-time close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier and co-author with the Lund and ETH attosecond groups; no direct connection to Katori, Ye, Halzen, Bloch, Greiner or Zoller apparent from profile, though I work in the same atomic-physics area as the clock and optical lattice candidates.
